title: The American Revolution
examples: What did the colonists object to about the taxes?
When exactly did the Declaration of Independence happen?
Who were the main people involved in the Revolution?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the American Revolution. This was a big change in history. The colonists felt they were treated unfairly by Great Britain.

items: They had no say in making those laws

explain.say: A concrete example is the Stamp Act. This required a tax stamp on printed materials. The colonists argued they should not pay taxes without having representatives in the British government.

draw.text: Stamp Act: Tax on paper goods

explain.say: Another example is the Townshend Acts. These acts placed taxes on items like glass and tea. The colonists believed that only their own elected assemblies could tax them.
The year 1776 was a very important time. This is when the colonies declared their separation from Great Britain. This marked the start of their fight for freedom.
The Declaration of Independence explained why the colonies were leaving. It listed many grievances against the King of Great Britain. It stated that all men are created equal.
In everyday life, when you buy something, you might pay sales tax. This is like the taxes the colonists protested. The principle is that you should know where the money goes.

faq.q: Why did the colonists get so angry about the taxes?
faq.a: The main issue was that they were being taxed by a body where they had no elected voice. They felt they had no representation in the British Parliament.
asks: Why was paying taxes without a say bad?

faq.q: What was the main point of the Declaration of Independence?
faq.a: It was a formal document stating that the thirteen colonies were free and independent states. It listed the reasons why they believed they needed to separate.
asks: What did the Declaration say about rights?

faq.q: Was the American Revolution just about money?
faq.a: No, it was also about ideas of self-governance and natural rights. They believed in the right to rule themselves.
asks: What were the core beliefs of the colonists?

faq.q: Did all the colonists agree on separating from Britain?
faq.a: No, there were many people who remained loyal to the British Crown. These people were sometimes called Loyalists.

faq.q: What does 'representation' mean in a government?
faq.a: It means that people elect representatives to speak for them in a governing body. This gives the people a voice in lawmaking.
asks: What is the meaning of representation?
Do we need representatives to vote?

facts: The colonists protested taxes like the Stamp Act.
The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
It stated that all men are created equal.
The goal was self-governance, not just lower taxes.
